deals.date_text: 20 December 2017 (agreement; Alychlo joined the board on 30 March 2018)
deals.evidence: Coucke betaalt 59,2 miljoen euro voor 74% van de aandelen in het Lotto Park.
deals.headline: Marc Coucke buys 74% of Anderlecht for EUR 59.2m
deals.seller: Roger Vanden Stock and the other selling shareholders
deals.summary: Coucke, through Alychlo and alongside Joris Ide, won the sale over Paul Gheysens and Alisher Usmanov. RTBF separately put the price at an estimated EUR 70m; the purchase later led to a criminal trial over undisclosed liabilities (February 2026).

deals.evidence: Les deux parties ont déjà convenu de régler cela dans une transaction commerciale d’environ 3 millions d’euros
deals.headline: Sellers and Alychlo settle 2017 price dispute for about EUR 3m
deals.seller: Selling shareholders of 2017 (statement by Etienne Davignon)
deals.summary: Buyer and sellers agreed a commercial settlement of about EUR 3m over information not disclosed at the sale; any valuation correction is paid by Alychlo to the club to strengthen its capital.

deals.evidence: Michael Verschueren y reprend les parts d'Alexandre Van Damme et Jo Van Biesbroeck.
deals.headline: Michael Verschueren takes over the minority stakes of Alexandre Van Damme and Jo Van Biesbroeck
deals.seller: Alexandre Van Damme and Jo Van Biesbroeck
deals.summary: Change among the minority shareholders; no price or percentage published.

deals.evidence: le conseil d'administration du RSCA a approuvé à l'unanimité une augmentation de capital de 5 millions d'euros
deals.headline: Board approves EUR 5m capital increase under Financial Fair Play
deals.summary: First step of the new management's recovery plan; the club did not name the subscribers.

deals.evidence: Met het kerstakkoord kochten Wouter Vandenhaute en financieel specialist Geert Duyck 26 % van Anderlecht voor 24 miljoen euro.
deals.headline: Mauvavie buys 26% of Anderlecht for EUR 24m in the 'Christmas agreement'
deals.summary: Part of a EUR 42m capital increase that also brought in Steven Buyse and Michael Lavrysen; 26% gives Mauvavie a blocking minority above the 25% threshold.

deals.evidence: Steven Buyse, de rechterhand van Duyck bij het investeringsfonds CVC, steekt 5 miljoen in de club.
deals.headline: Steven Buyse puts EUR 5m into Anderlecht
deals.summary: Buyse, described by Bruzz as Geert Duyck's right hand at CVC, invested in a personal capacity as part of the 2021 capital increase.

deals.evidence: In het kerstakkoord zetten Coucke en Ide 18 miljoen euro schulden om in kapitaal met daar bovenop 11 miljoen verse kapitaalinbreng.
deals.headline: Coucke and Ide convert EUR 18m of loans into equity
deals.summary: In the same agreement Coucke and Ide added EUR 11m of fresh capital, and Coucke took a further EUR 33m of claims off the balance sheet under a return-to-better-fortune clause, turning negative equity of EUR 52m into positive equity of EUR 50m.

deals.evidence: Michael Verschueren en Johan Beerlandt hebben hun aandelen verkocht aan hoofdaandeelhouder Marc Coucke.
deals.headline: Verschueren and Beerlandt sell their minority shares to Coucke
deals.summary: Settled the dispute with the minority shareholders over the capital increase; Verschueren stayed on the board.

deals.evidence: Vandenhaute bereikte een akkoord met Geert Duyck, zijn vennoot bij Mauvavie, over de verkoop van al zijn aandelen.
deals.headline: Vandenhaute sells his Mauvavie shares to Geert Duyck and leaves Anderlecht
deals.summary: Indirect change: Mauvavie remains a shareholder of the club with Duyck and Erik Watte; Vandenhaute keeps no direct or indirect interest and leaves the board.

wages.source_name: Royal Sporting Club Anderlecht NV, annual accounts to 30 June 2025 (National Bank of Belgium, Central Balance Sheet Office)

name: Royal Sporting Club Anderlecht
notes: Revenue is the club's stated operating revenue (bedrijfsopbrengsten) for 2024-25, EUR 111m; the filed accounts give EUR 111,008,609, of which turnover (omzet) EUR 91,304,983 and other operating income (mainly transfer gains) EUR 19,517,775; net profit EUR 109,593 (2023-24: operating revenue EUR 105,745,990, net profit EUR 1,588,290). The wages, operating and pre-tax figures come from the filed accounts PDF at the National Bank of Belgium (financial year 1 July 2024 - 30 June 2025, approved 27 November 2025); the PDF omits the shareholder-structure section, so no registry source gives current stakes. Stakes are as reported in January 2022 (De Rijkste Belgen) after the December 2021 recapitalisation: Coucke and Ide 59% combined, Mauvavie 26%, traditional minority shareholders 7%. A November 2025 football-news report (voetbalbelgie.be, not citable) gives Coucke 56.6%, Mauvavie 26.29%, Joris Ide 6%, Steven Buyse 5.48%, Michael Lavrysen 2.19%, Etienne Davignon 1.9% and Claire and Julie Vanden Stock 1%. No primary or reputable page confirms those. Coucke's 2017 purchase: VRT/Sporza (2026) say EUR 59.2m for 74%; RTBF gives an 'estimated' EUR 70m for 74%. No institutional, PE, sovereign or fund investor appears in any source: Duyck and Buyse are CVC executives investing personally (Made in, BRUZZ). Patrick Vermeulen (Ascot House Advisers) joined the board in September 2025 representing Buyse and Lavrysen (VRT). Stadium capacity left blank: only aggregators state it (21,500 vs 22,500), and they disagree. The 2023-24 club release gives only a 98% average occupancy, not an attendance figure. No published valuation (Anderlecht is outside Football Benchmark's top-32 list; no Forbes or Sportico figure). The club names the stadium Lotto Park (naming deal with the National Lottery, extended in 2023). Adidas replaced JOMA as kit supplier from 2026-27. City: the club is in the municipality of Anderlecht, Brussels-Capital Region.

ownership_summary: Majority-owned by Marc Coucke through his investment company Alychlo NV, which agreed in December 2017 to buy 74% from Roger Vanden Stock and the other selling shareholders for EUR 59.2m. After the December 2021 recapitalisation Coucke and his partner Joris Ide held 59%, Mauvavie (the vehicle of Geert Duyck and Erik Watte, and of Wouter Vandenhaute until he sold out to Duyck in November 2025) 26%, and the traditional minority shareholders 7%; Steven Buyse and Michael Lavrysen also came in as private investors. The shareholders are individuals and their holding companies, not funds: Duyck and Buyse are CVC executives but invested in a personal capacity.
